core.title: Coordinate durable work only through the workflow coordination records
core.given: The workflow profile is active (durable coordination records live in the separate coordination root) and you act as any seat — main, coordinator, driver or operator — including while implementing an assigned task, launching a seat or creating initial records.
core.when: You take any workflow step: start or resume, implement and prove a task, change task or seat state, message, hand over, transfer, review, launch or retire a seat.
core.then: Change task, seat, checkpoint, handover and thread records only through the installed workflow coordination tool, acting from what those records currently say (read them before acting).
prefer: Before workflow action, run the installed coordination tool's help command to discover the installed commands and current syntax; treat that help output as the command authority.

Read the task, seat, checkpoint and thread records before acting; start or resume from the current seat, checkpoint, assigned tasks and relevant threads. A replacement agent resumes from those records and never depends on a conversation with its predecessor.

Driver: start only your assigned ready task; treat its done_when criteria as the delivery scope and implement the smallest sufficient change: prefer existing repository patterns, components, dependencies, contracts and abstractions; when multiple implementations are correct, choose the smallest effective change that agrees with the existing system; do not redesign adjacent systems, introduce generalized infrastructure, add dependencies, create abstractions for hypothetical future requirements, or perform unrelated cleanup merely because the opportunity was discovered; remove speculative scope not required for correctness; broaden only when a done_when criterion requires it, the current design cannot correctly satisfy the task without it, or the broader change is necessary to resolve a verified blocker. Work criterion by criterion, continuing from the next unmet done_when criterion through implementation, verification and proof: complete the required implementation, run the relevant tests and the stack's convention checks, correct failures caused by your work, record proof for every done_when criterion, move the task to review and send your coordinator a result. Continue until the task is review-ready (implementation and verification complete, proof on every criterion, task in review, coordinator has the result) or explicitly blocked.
If completion is impossible, block explicitly: record the blocker, checkpoint the exact current state and next action, and notify the coordinator.

At a responsibility boundary (shared vocabulary, endpoint shape, contracts, artifact ownership or another participant's responsibility), send the concrete boundary question to your coordinator. The coordinator aligns directly with affected coordinators through the existing durable thread mechanism, resolves only the minimum shared vocabulary, interface, ownership or responsibility split needed for the current work, prefers an existing convention or contract over inventing one, records the agreement in a relevant thread and communicates the result back to affected drivers.

Route messages: drivers send normal work messages to their coordinator (never directly to the operator or main seat); coordinators may escalate a concrete decision or incident directly to the operator; main seats are the normal repository-main integration gateway to the operator; a receipt or result addresses the seat that made the request, not every historical participant in the thread.

Drivers hand work back to their named coordinator for integration and validation; the named coordinator hands a reviewed integration candidate to main; only main completes normal integration-to-main gates and publication.

Topology for new projects: the main seat is the sole primary-checkout and main-branch coordinator; a named integration coordinator works only from its own linked integration branch and worktree and integrates bounded driver delivery rather than acting as a hidden feature driver; a driver it coordinates derives its governed base from that exact integration head, while a main-coordinated driver derives from main. Reject nested coordinator lineage, mismatched base/worktree placement and ambiguous placement rather than guessing.

Transfer active task accountability only through the coordination tool's transfer operation. The current coordinator may transfer; main may only with one applicable immutable transfer-authorization message of the typed authorization construct the collaboration idiom defines (idiom.collaboration#task_transfer_authorization), from the human operator, whose project, task, from, to, reason and exact target branch/head match the requested transfer before mutation (only the human operator's coordination address may create that typed authorization). Accept only main or a valid named integration coordinator as target and atomically derive the new governed base from the accepted target head. Provenance (from/to/reason/exact-head/effective-time) is append-only and prior task, phase, review and message evidence stays attributable. Reject same-target, duplicate, nested, mismatched, unauthorized or manually rewritten transfers. A transfer never moves or changes any seat, branch, runtime binding, worktree, dirty state or evidence artifact.

Context handover, every seat (main, coordinator, driver, operator): begin at 80% and no later than 90% context usage, depending on context (not a single fixed threshold). The primary path, which every seat self-services, is same-session compaction: validate and record the handover/checkpoint, pass the recovery bundle as the compaction summary, and continue in the same session and runtime binding. If compaction is unavailable, fails an invariant, or the session is stuck, the workflow tooling uses its verified new-session successor path as the fail-closed fallback; operator intervention is fallback-only.

To hand over: finish or cleanly undo the current atomic step (commit, post, receipt) and start nothing new; write the handover using the template, validate it with the coordination tool's handover check, fix every reported problem, and record it through the coordination tool. The seat's handover record is the one durable handover record; it sits beside the checkpoint and never replaces it. On the fallback path the old session then makes no further tool calls and a fresh session bound to the same seat continues; after compaction the same session continues.

Handover content: point to toolkit conventions, never restate or override them; list open items only, use exact IDs and mark state [verified|assumed]; 150 lines is a ceiling, not a target. Recording rejects a missing or malformed header or runtime line, a missing, duplicate or out-of-order section, more than 150 lines, a wrong supersedes value, and vague references without an exact identifier (details in the verifier's handover check).

Handover template: a header line in the identity-header syntax of the stack's header idiom (urn.header#handover_identity: the handover record's identity — seat address, UTC timestamp, handover id, and the supersedes id or none) and a runtime line in the runtime-header syntax (urn.header#handover_runtime: the runtime application and its session, the agent's session id, the model provider/model, and the context-usage percentage), then four sections in order — 1. Seat, authority, toolkit and hazards: the seat (address with role, project, reports-to address, directs addresses or none); the worktree (path, branch, commit id, clean or dirty with the dirty files); the toolkit in force in this worktree (the coordination tool's and the stack's versions, whether declared=locked=installed versions agree — with detail when not current — and the runtime binding version or unverified); governing conventions for the current phase as pointers only; profile and ratchet state, with activated ratchets listed and never modified; authorizations in force (scope, granting address, reference message id, expiry timestamp or never); seat-specific constraints beyond the instruction file; hazards, known bugs and workarounds; dead ends (tried, failed, do not repeat) each with a reference, or none. 2. Open work and in-flight operations: per open task one line (project and task id, status/phase, assignee address, verified or assumed, an exact reference such as pull request/commit/running session, last evidence message id, one-line state); each in-flight operation (operation, start timestamp, the exact check command, retry-safe yes/no/why); session-only knowledge not recorded in the coordination desk, or none. 3. Dependencies in both directions: waiting on (what, address, since timestamp, reference message id, follow-up time); owed by me (what, to address, due timestamp, reference message id); decision pending (question, owner address, options with a recommendation, reference); received not yet acted on (message id, from address, needed action); or none per subsection. 4. Resume procedure and next actions: verify first — the seat's status and every open task read from the coordination records; the worktree's version-control status and latest commit; the installed toolkit versions in the worktree checked against section 1 (a mismatch is a discrepancy to report, never self-upgraded); every in-flight check command run — then, in order: read the inbox and receipt every pending message that lacks this seat's receipt, then concrete next actions with exact ids.

Resuming session: read the instruction file, then show the recorded handover through the coordination tool, run the handover's verification, reconcile it with the live coordination desk (the desk wins), reconcile your inbox, report 'RESUMED; verified N/M; discrepancies: ...' through your normal reporting route, and continue. Read a convention when its phase is acted on, not all on resume.

Use the coordination tool's scope scouting only when repository scope is genuinely unclear or candidate files are numerous; use its focus check only before a likely scope expansion (new dependency, generalized abstraction, persistent schema, architecture change, adjacent refactor, unrelated defect). These are read-only judgment-helper results that advise scope; they do not own correctness or completion.

Launching a seat: new seats do not pin a model. The coordination desk's model portfolio lists launchable candidates ordered strongest to weakest; for ordinary launches ask the model-selection helper for the weakest available model sufficient for the seat's current active work; if model selection is unavailable or low-confidence, use the strongest available configured model.

Final review (coordinator): between phases, let the next phase consume and semantically challenge the prior one while the stack's active conventions enforce deterministically; reserve the explicit independent semantic reviewer (behavioral review: final semantic reconciliation after deterministic gates, before review -> done) for the final integration boundary. After the driver moves the task to review, run the deterministic convention gates in the delivery worktree before launching the reviewer. Only after they pass may the judgment helper answer bounded routing questions: classify the review surface as LOCAL, ASSEMBLED, JOURNEY or SYSTEM with routing signals (behavior-affecting vs behavior-preserving intent, highest relevant proof boundary, cross-path scope, consequence, reconciliation shape, runtime observability, confidence); treat low-confidence routing as SYSTEM. Map the routing result through the model portfolio to a reviewer model, create a task-scoped reviewer responsibility in the delivery worktree, and supply inputs in this order: task criteria/source; relevant plan artifacts; deterministic gate evidence; executable proof; runtime/worktree; then implementation/diff context. Include the complete installed behavioral-review convention in the reviewer prompt as the authoritative method — the stack's convention set owns the review method; the workflow owns routing, reviewer allocation, durable evidence and lifecycle enforcement.

Reviewer: record durable structured evidence — intent sources, expected behavior, exercised boundary and evidence, observed behavior, reconciliation findings, a decision of APPROVE, RETURN or ESCALATE, rationale and confidence — and never mutate task state. Coordinator: APPROVE makes the current clean delivery commit eligible for completion; on RETURN move review back to in_progress; on ESCALATE leave the task in the review or explicitly block it until authoritative intent is resolved. Only the coordinator moves review to done, and only when the latest behavioral-review attempt is complete, records APPROVE and matches the current clean delivery commit.

Retiring a driver seat (the final housekeeping step for an idle driver seat, delegated to the stack's tooling): install the repository's local dependencies in a driver worktree before working in or retiring it. A coordinator retires the assignee through the coordination tool's completion operation only when every task assigned to that driver in the project is done and the seat is intentionally being retired; the operation delegates worktree and delivery-branch cleanup to the stack's governed cleanup command and never resolves that command from the seat worktree's own copy, which may pin an older toolkit that refuses its own retirement. A failed retirement leaves the task in review and writes a blocked checkpoint for investigation.
avoid: Inventing flags, inferring command forms from memory, or relying on an older agent's instructions.

Treating terminal pane history, a multiplexer, an optional judgment helper or an agent's private memory as durable coordination state; rewriting task records directly (e.g. to transfer accountability).

Posting, approving or making a decision while claiming the human operator's coordination address (the human authority, not an autonomous agent identity) unless the human operator actually supplied it.

A driver independently redefining a shared contract; using boundary coordination to redesign adjacent systems or solve hypothetical future needs; reopening a settled boundary decision without concrete implementation evidence that it cannot satisfy the task.

Intentionally ending an autonomous work turn on an assigned in_progress task while required work remains actionable; treating successful code generation as task completion; silently leaving actionable required work unfinished.
Removing a worktree, deleting a delivery branch or forcing cleanup through raw version-control commands; retiring a seat's assignee while that driver still has undone tasks in the project.
Adding a writer/reviewer pair after every development phase; invoking the semantic reviewer while a strict gate is red (return the discrepancy to the appropriate implementation phase instead).
Letting the judgment helper approve a delivery, decide semantic correctness, mutate task state or redefine intent; duplicating the behavioral-review methodology in the workflow convention.
Introducing an automatic merge executor, branch graph, daemon or scheduler as part of this workflow.
Self-upgrading the toolkit when installed versions on resume differ from the handover (report it as a discrepancy).
unless: A broader change is permitted when a done_when criterion requires it, the current design cannot correctly satisfy the task without it, or it is necessary to resolve a verified blocker.
A driver waiting on a boundary decision continues any independent required work that remains actionable; mark the task blocked only when the unresolved decision prevents further meaningful progress.
A task may be completed normally without retiring its assignee when that driver still has work (a driver seat may own more than one task).
A live host may notify an agent to inspect its seat, but it never owns the durable state.
An optional scouting, focus, final-review-routing or model-selection judgment may advise execution, but never owns task state, proof, correctness or completion authority.
A legacy coordination desk without a model portfolio may continue to use its pinned seat agent.
Legacy seat, task and thread identities remain readable without rename or mutation.
core.why: A seat owns its runtime binding, branch and worktree, a task its delivery state and proof, a thread its conversation; keeping these durable records as the single source of truth lets any replacement agent resume and keeps evidence attributable, which panes, private memory and advisory judgments cannot.
evidence: Every change to task, seat, checkpoint, handover or thread records is attributable to a coordination-tool invocation; no hand-edited task records and no raw version-control worktree/branch removal in seat worktrees.

review -> done happened only by the coordinator when the latest behavioral-review attempt is complete, records APPROVE and matches the current clean delivery commit (proves the review occurred and applies to this delivery, not that its judgment is correct).
A review-ready task has completed implementation and verification, proof on every done_when criterion, is in review, and the coordinator has a result message; otherwise it is explicitly blocked.
A recorded handover passed the coordination tool's handover check; the resuming session reported 'RESUMED; verified N/M; discrepancies: ...' through its normal route.
A blocked task carries the blocker, a checkpoint with exact state and next action, and a coordinator notification.
Boundary agreements are recorded in the relevant thread and communicated to affected drivers.

Task transfers carry append-only from/to/reason/exact-head/effective-time provenance with prior task, phase, review and message evidence still attributable; main-initiated transfers cite a matching operator transfer-authorization message of the collaboration idiom's typed authorization construct (idiom.collaboration#task_transfer_authorization).
A reviewer was launched only after green deterministic gates and its prompt included the complete installed behavioral-review convention.
verification: Handover recording check (deterministic): rejects a missing or malformed header or runtime line — the concrete identity and runtime-line syntaxes come from the profile's header idiom (urn.header#handover_identity, urn.header#handover_runtime); a missing, duplicate or out-of-order section; more than 150 lines; a supersedes value other than the recorded handover id (or none when none is recorded); and vague references — the words latest, newest, most recent, and that/this/those/these/same/previous/earlier/above/last/aforementioned followed by PR, pull request, task, thread, message, commit, branch, handover, session, issue or release without an exact identifier (one containing a digit, @ or /).

Done gate (deterministic, repositories explicitly governed by the workflow profile): review -> done is prevented unless the latest behavioral-review attempt is complete, records APPROVE and matches the current clean delivery commit. These checks prove that the required review occurred and applies to the delivery being completed; they do not prove the reviewer's semantic judgment is correct.

Transfer and topology validation (deterministic): transfers that are same-target, duplicate, nested, mismatched, unauthorized or manually rewritten are rejected; nested coordinator lineage, mismatched base/worktree placement and ambiguous placement are rejected. The validator identities are realization details of the checking tool.

Attribution of record changes (observer-based, not deterministic): every change to task, seat, checkpoint, handover or thread records must be attributable to a coordination-tool invocation — no hand-edited records, no raw version-control worktree/branch removal in seat worktrees. Checking this needs an observer of coordination-tool invocations, seat launches, direct record edits and raw version-control cleanup in seat worktrees.

values: coordination record in the coordination root (task, seat, checkpoint, handover, thread)

fires: A driver is implementing an assigned in_progress task and is about to end its turn or declare the work done.
A seat starts or resumes work, or an agent creates initial workflow records or launches a seat that has no assigned task yet.
A coordinator is about to move a task from review to done, transfer it, or retire its driver seat.
Any seat reaches 80–90% context usage and must hand over.
A driver hits a shared vocabulary, endpoint shape, contract or ownership question with another seat or project.
Workflow is preparing to launch the final behavioral reviewer for a delivery.
doesNotFire: The repository is not governed by the workflow profile.

profileRequirements.meaning: The installed CLI that owns and mutates the durable workflow coordination records (task, seat, checkpoint, handover, thread); only it may change them, and its help output is the command authority.
profileRequirements.bunValue: atdd-flow — invoked as `atdd-flow` (or `bunx atdd-flow --help` when the executable is project-local and not on PATH); transfer via `atdd-flow task transfer`, handover via `atdd-flow handover <address> --check --file <path>` / `--file <path>`, show via `atdd-flow handover show <address>`, retirement via `atdd-flow task done <project> <task> --by <coordinator> --retire-assignee`

profileRequirements.meaning: The command/tool that runs the stack's deterministic convention checks and gates, which must be green before the behavioral reviewer is launched and which enforces deterministically between phases. It is only the convention-check runner; worktree/branch cleanup at retirement is tooling.commands#worktree_cleanup.
profileRequirements.bunValue: atdd-bun — runs the stack's convention checks and deterministic gates ('run the relevant tests and ATDD Bun checks', 'the deterministic ATDD Bun gates in the delivery worktree', 'active ATDD Bun conventions enforce deterministically')

profileRequirements.meaning: Root of the separate workflow coordination repository holding the durable coordination records, distinct from the source/test/plan roots; the workflow-profile observer resolves against it. The record-kind layout and file-name patterns below it come from layout.locations#coordination_records, suffix.coordination_record and layout.locations#model_portfolio, not from this key.

profileRequirements.meaning: File-name pattern of the durable coordination record kinds; the activation globs for record files resolve through this key.

profileRequirements.meaning: How seat addresses are written for the main seat, driver seats and named integration coordinators, and the reserved human-operator coordination address that no autonomous agent may claim.

profileRequirements.meaning: The typed authorization message construct a main-initiated task transfer must cite: the immutable transfer-authorization message type that only the reserved human-operator coordination address may create, whose fields (project, task, from, to, reason, exact target branch/head) must match the requested transfer before mutation. Supplies the concrete idiom for the core's typed-authorization requirement; the general authorization conditions stay in the core.
profileRequirements.bunValue: task-transfer-authorization/v1 — one applicable immutable `operator@desk` message whose project, task, from, to, reason and exact target branch/head match the requested transfer before mutation (only `operator@desk` may create that typed authorization)

profileRequirements.meaning: The handover record's identity header-line syntax: the record keyword and the seat address, UTC timestamp, handover id, and supersedes id (or none) — the concrete form of the core's required, format-validated header line.

The handover record's runtime-line syntax: the runtime application and its session binding, the agent's session id, the model provider/model, and the context-usage percentage — the concrete form of the core's required, format-validated runtime line.
Where the coordination desk's model-portfolio record (launchable model candidates ordered strongest to weakest, used for seat launches and reviewer-model mapping) lives.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the Desk's models.yaml (**/models.yaml), ordered strongest to weakest

profileRequirements.meaning: The governed command that performs worktree and delivery-branch cleanup when a driver seat is retired, and how it is resolved — never from the retiring seat worktree's own potentially stale copy.

Handover template (complete concrete template of this realization):
HANDOVER <seat-address> | <UTC ts> | handover-id <id> | supersedes <id|none>
Runtime: <application> <session>:<pane> | <agent> session <id> | model <provider/model> | context <NN>%
1. SEAT, AUTHORITY, TOOLKIT AND HAZARDS
- Seat: <address> (<role>), project <project>; reports to <addr>; directs <addrs|none>
- Worktree: <path> @ <branch> <sha> (<clean | dirty: files>)
- Toolkit in force (this worktree): Flow <ver> / Bun <ver> | declared=locked=installed: <yes | NOT CURRENT: detail> | runtime binding: <Flow ver | unverified>
- Governing conventions for current phase: <convention ids> (pointers only)
- Profile/ratchet state: <profile> <reject-new|strict> | activated ratchets (never modify): <list|none>
- Authorizations in force: <scope> | granted by <addr> | ref <msg-id> | expires <ts|never>
- Seat-specific constraints (beyond the instruction file): <list|none>
- Hazards / known bugs / workarounds: <list|none>
- Dead ends (tried, failed, do not repeat): <what> | ref <id> (or none)
2. OPEN WORK AND IN-FLIGHT OPERATIONS
- <project>/<task-id> | <status/phase> | assignee <addr> | [verified|assumed]
  ref: <PR#/sha/pane>; last evidence <msg-id>; state: <one line>
- IN-FLIGHT: <operation> | started <ts> | check: <exact command> | retry-safe: <yes|no|why>
- Session-only knowledge: <facts learned, not recorded in Desk> (or none)
3. DEPENDENCIES (both directions)
- WAITING ON: <what> | <addr> | since <ts> | ref <msg-id> | follow up at <ts>
- OWED BY ME: <what> | to <addr> | due <ts> | ref <msg-id>
- DECISION PENDING: <question> | owner <addr> | options A/B + recommendation | ref <id>
- RECEIVED, NOT YET ACTED ON: <msg-id> | from <addr> | needed action
(or: none, per subsection)
4. RESUME PROCEDURE AND NEXT ACTIONS
Verify first:
- atdd-flow status seat <address>
- atdd-flow task open <project> <task-id>   (each open task)
- git -C <worktree> status && git log -1
- installed toolkit versions in <worktree> match section 1 (mismatch = discrepancy; report, do not self-upgrade)
- <each IN-FLIGHT check command>
Then, in order:
1. Read inbox; receipt pending messages lacking my receipt.
2. <concrete action with exact IDs>

neutralityNotes: This is a coach/workflow convention, so its subject matter is coordination vocabulary (seat, coordinator, driver, main, operator, desk, task, checkpoint, handover, thread, done_when, review states), retained in the core as the convention's own domain terms rather than stack machinery. Revision fixes this round: the typed transfer-authorization message construct is supplied through idiom.collaboration#task_transfer_authorization and connected to the core's typed-authorization requirement in prefer[8] and evidence[6], with the general authorization conditions (immutability, matching fields, operator-only creation, before-mutation timing) kept in the core; the concrete handover identity-header and runtime-line syntaxes are supplied through urn.header#handover_identity and urn.header#handover_runtime and connected to core prefer[12] and the handover recording check, leaving the general content requirements and rejection rules in the core. No new keys were proposed (all are entries of existing v3 map keys). Earlier revision fixes retained: the sidecar's shared smallest-sufficient-change policy (policy.phase-loop) is carried in full, neutrally, inside core prefer[2]; the handover template's neutral requirements (UTC timestamp, runtime line, authorizations with grantor/reference/expiry, dependency since/follow-up/due fields, declared=locked=installed status, never modifying activated ratchets, verify-first of each open task and in-flight command, receipting pending messages) are all in core prefer[12], with the complete concrete Bun template preserved verbatim in bunOnly; retirement keeps only the neutral never-the-seat-worktree's-copy rule (no primary-checkout-only strengthening), with the full Bun resolution order in tooling.commands#worktree_cleanup; enforcement.runner is restricted to convention checks; the coordination root (roots.coordination) is separated from coordination layout (layout.locations#coordination_records), record file patterns (suffix.coordination_record) and model-portfolio location (layout.locations#model_portfolio), and seat-address/integration-branch idioms (idiom.collaboration#seat_address, idiom.collaboration#integration_branch) let other stacks instantiate the same roles. Remaining realization detail: the coordination CLI name and command syntax, the judgment helper, the record format (YAML) and file names, the session/pane/compaction machinery, the sister behavioral-review convention id, the raw-VCS name, and the toolkit resolution order — all carried in bunOnly or supplied by profile entries. Numeric thresholds (80–90% context, 150-line handover ceiling) and the vague-reference word lists are tool-neutral and kept in the core. The Bun text itself records that this convention bundles several obligations slated for splitting; the neutral core preserves the bundle faithfully rather than pre-splitting it, and the pending-compaction caveat stays realization-side.
